answer: Each epoch pairs each identity with a random stranger for a live uniqueness challenge: each side answers from its own work and co-signs a transcript. The plume of signed transcripts is published in an open meadow for audit, and a zephyr check re-pairs samples without warning. Stand-in rental is the named failure mode: a stand-in covering a second identity leaves matching timing on two transcripts, and both are frozen. The k-th fake still needs its own respondent at 20 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 20,000 credits with no reuse, while an honest agent spends one hour once.
